record.paper_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can physical-layer security techniques be used to provide message integrity for satellite communication systems, so that man-in-the-middle style attacks that intercept, modify, and retransmit satellite-to-user or user-to-satellite signals can be detected reliably before corrupted information is accepted or processed?

evidence.quote: Message manipulation detection techniques using PLS are not considered in the literature yet for any wireless communication. Integrity violation attacks such as man-in-the-middle intercept the message during transmission, modify it or manipulate it, and then re-transmit it.

Satellite systems are vulnerable to these attacks where adversaries can intercept the signal sent by satellite to the terrestrial user or vice-versa and manipulate it either to disturb the service or to get access by exploiting these messages. PLS techniques to achieve integrity needs to be investigated using different wireless signals, including satellite systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a satellite communication system consisting of a satellite transmitter and a terrestrial user (or vice versa) communicating over a wireless channel. An adversary positioned between the two legitimate parties may carry out an integrity-violation (man-in-the-middle) attack by intercepting the transmitted signal, modifying or manipulating the carried message, and retransmitting the altered signal to the intended receiver, with the goal of disrupting service or gaining unauthorized access.

Design and analyze physical-layer security (PLS) mechanisms — that is, techniques that exploit physical characteristics of the wireless transmission (such as channel state information, channel reciprocity, propagation effects, noise statistics, hardware imperfections, or signal-level fingerprints) rather than upper-layer cryptography — that provide message integrity for such satellite links. Specifically:

1. Formulate a model of the legitimate satellite-to-user (and user-to-satellite) channel and of an active man-in-the-middle adversary capable of intercepting, modifying, and retransmitting signals.
2. Propose PLS-based message-manipulation detection schemes that allow the legitimate receiver to decide, before accepting or processing the received message, whether the signal has been tampered with in transit.
3. Establish quantitative guarantees (e.g., detection probability, false-alarm probability, and the range of adversary capabilities under which detection is reliable) for the proposed schemes in the satellite setting, accounting for the long propagation distances, large path loss, Doppler effects, and atmospheric impairments characteristic of satellite links.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on physical-layer security for satellite communications (2024–2025) continue to list PLS-based message-integrity / manipulation-detection mechanisms against man-in-the-middle attacks as an open research direction. Some partial approaches (e.g., exploiting atmospheric effects, PUF-based cross-layer frameworks combining DSFH at the physical layer) have been proposed for related authentication and MITM mitigation tasks, but a general PLS-based integrity-detection methodology for satellite links with quantitative guarantees has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Physical layer security in satellite communication: State-of-the-art and open problems (IET Communications, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists PLS-based integrity / message manipulation detection for satellite communication as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: PLS-based message integrity for satellite communications remains an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: Review of Physical Layer Security in Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks (MDPI Electronics, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses PLS techniques for satellite-terrestrial networks; integrity protection via PLS is highlighted as an emerging issue rather than a solved one.
status_evidence.claim: Integrity protection via PLS in satellite-terrestrial networks is not yet solved.

status_evidence.title: Advanced security framework for low Earth orbit satellites (EURASIP JWCN, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a cross-layer framework combining PUF-based mutual authentication with dynamic seed frequency hopping at the physical layer to counter MITM and spoofing attacks on LEO satellites.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solutions targeting MITM in satellite links exist but do not provide a general PLS-based integrity-detection guarantee.
